connections.title: Connect your database
connections.body: This app talks to your databases over ODBC. Click Add connection — DSNs already installed on this PC are detected automatically and listed for you. Save one and it appears as a badge in the top bar.

queryTemplate.title: Query with a template
queryTemplate.body: Pick the connection you saved in the row above. A Template menu appears when ready-made quick-searches exist for it — choose one, fill the criteria (dates with a red * are required), then press Run. The SQL is generated for you.

scriptTemplate.title: Analyze with a template script
scriptTemplate.body: Open the Script tab and pick a script such as analyze-mesa-yield from the Template menu: it loads into the editor. Hit Run and the charts open in your browser, with the file saved to your Downloads folder.

hero.lead: One local app for every step with your ODBC data — connect, query without SQL, analyze, chart and ask the built-in AI assistant.

demo.aiAnswer: West trails the regional average by 29%, and South is next. Want a bar chart of revenue against average?

connect.title: Connect once. Query without SQL.
connect.body: Add an ODBC DSN, a connection string or an Access file, then run a ready-made quick-search — dates, lots, branches — and the SQL is written for you. Prefer raw SQL? The read-only SELECT editor is right there, and results land in the grid below.

charts.title: See the shape of it.
charts.body: The Analyze tab turns results into bar, pie, trend, scatter, histogram, box or KPI charts — pick an X and a Y axis and the options adapt. Drag columns together in the Dashboard view, snapshot results into the local warehouse, or pin the charts you keep coming back to.

scripts.title: Analyze it your way.
scripts.body: Write a Python or JavaScript script in the Analyze tab and run it over every row in the grid — template scripts included — and watch stdout stream in live. Copy the output, or export to Excel, CSV or SAS XPT.

ai.title: Ask for a second pair of eyes.
ai.body: The AI assistant sits on the Query and Analyze tabs and writes SQL, drafts scripts or builds charts in sql, script or chart mode. Point it at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — your key stays in the Windows Credential Manager.

final.lead: Connections stay on this machine, queries are read-only by default, and nothing leaves your PC unless you export it. No internet needed.
